newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Hard-up Kazakh pensioners protest rising costs.
newsitem.headline: Hard-up Kazakh pensioners protest rising costs.

text.p: Hundreds of hard-up pensioners in Kazakhstan, their meagre pensions unable to meet rising state charges for rents and utilities, held an unsanctioned demonstration in the capital Almaty on Friday.
The elderly protesters, who gathered in front of parliament, carried placards declaring "Do not humiliate us with poverty" and "Increased tariffs mean death".
The pensioners carried red Soviet flags in a sign of nostalgia for the communist past, before the Soviet Union collapsed and Kazakhstan became an independent state.
They slammed the government for the hike in rents and payments for utilities.
"Why do the president and government condemn the people to hunger, cold and poverty?" one pensioner shouted through a loudspeaker.
Police estimated the crowd at around 1,500, a large gathering in a country where President Nursultan Nazarbayev enjoys sweeping executive powers and tolerates little dissent.
Pensions in Almaty average around 3,000 tenge ($40), while rent and utilities for a medium-sized flat now cost 2,500 tenge ($33) a month.

The government of the resource-rich Central Asian state, five times the size of France, says it has managed to attract billions of dollars in foreign investment but market economic reforms have passed by much of the 16.9 million population.

"Nazarbayev, you are not the master but the servant of the people. Who gave you the right to sell the property of the country?" one of the speakers said, criticising the republic's fast-track privatisations.
